def demolition_winners(towers):
    """
    Two players, 'A' and 'B', take turns demolishing blocks in a row of
    towers.

    Each tower is a non-empty string of characters 'A' and 'B' read from the
    ground up (towers[i][0] is the bottom block). On their turn a player must
    choose one block of their own letter in any tower and demolish it; that
    block and every block above it in the same tower are removed. A player
    with no legal move on their turn loses. Both players play optimally.

    Return a two-character string XY, where X is the winner ('A' or 'B') of
    the game in which A moves first, and Y is the winner of the game in
    which B moves first.

    Input domain: 1 <= len(towers) <= 60, and each tower is a string of
    'A'/'B' characters with 1 <= len(tower) <= 60. (The joint game state
    space is up to 61**60, so naive search is astronomically slow.)

    >>> demolition_winners(["AB"])
    'AA'
    >>> demolition_winners(["A", "B"])
    'BA'
    >>> demolition_winners(["AB", "B"])
    'BB'
    """
